packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-04 - unverified first reading from images only

EXPOSURE / PROCEDURE NOTES
- Nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification of the work or a
  prior reading. Only my brief and PROMPT.md were read.
- The only identifying text I saw is a modern pencil shelfmark on the face 2
  image (image-023/024, lower margin): "Stams, STA, Frg. 209v". It names the
  holding and folio, not the text. I did not use it to identify the content.
- Beyond the rules: the harness dropped several image views (from both
  overviews image-001 and image-014, and from several tiles), so I couldn't
  see them directly. To read those tiles I wrote small PIL scripts. They crop
  regions from the supplied tiles, boost contrast (some use the blue channel
  plus equalization) and enlarge them. The scripts and outputs are in my
  session scratchpad and touch no packet file. I also stitched reduced
  top-strip views of each face from the tiles to stand in for the overviews.
  No web, catalogue or edition was used.
- Line numbers below are counted from the first text line visible in the
  named tile (written lines only, not ruling). They are approximate where
  tiles overlap. Lines repeated across overlapping tiles are given once,
  merged, with the tiles named.

LAYOUT SURVEY (observations)
- Two faces, each an opening of two pages across a central fold (bifolium).
  The fold area has stitching holes and paper/parchment strips (binding
  reuse). Face 1 = image-001 overview + tiles image-002..013. Face 2 =
  image-014 overview + tiles image-015..026.
- One column per page, about 20 written lines per page, ruled in red, written
  in a formal gothic textualis book hand. Black text with red rubrics. There
  are red-and-blue penwork initials with scalloped/curled red filigree, and
  small red-touched capitals.
- Face 2 left page: a drawn shield/coat of arms (ink and wash) sits in the
  upper left margin (image-015). A large filigree initial X (blue with red
  penwork) is at image-019/023. Lower margin blank; pencil shelfmark.
- Face 2 right page: a blue O initial with red filigree (image-021/025).
  Rubric abbreviations: R. (responsory), V. (versicle), a. (antiphona),
  Cap. (capitulum), Or./Coll./Colla (prayer), "Ad ... a.", "In laud.",
  "Ad horas", "Ad iii cap.", "Ad vi. cap.".
- Face 1 left page: very rubric-dense and badly faded/abraded, mostly short
  incipits with rubrics (Coll., Cap., Ad v[esperas]?, R., V., Com., "In
  uigilia"). A large O initial in the lower part (image-006/010).
- Face 1 right page: a large hole/loss at the top lines (image-004/005).
  Text below is faded. A filigree initial (I or J?) is mid-page at
  image-008, with a short black-ink display word "In ii. noc(turno)?" lower
  down (image-008/012).
- Tentative interpretation (not an identification): this looks like
  liturgical office text (breviary type). It has chant/prayer incipits with
  rubrics, plus at least one block of continuous lesson-like prose (face 2
  left page). No commentary or glosses are visible, and there are no
  interlinear glosses.

AREAS SELECTED
- Face 2 left page, lines 1-20: continuous prose block plus rubric (best
  preserved stretch of prose).
- Face 2 right page, lines 1-20: continuous office text with rubrics (best
  preserved overall).
- Face 1 left page: scattered rubric/incipit lines (partial only).
- Face 1 right page: a few lines around the initial and "In ii. noc." (partial
  only).
UNREAD / POORLY READ: most of face 1 (both pages) beyond the fragments below.
The ink there is abraded to ghosts. UV or multispectral imaging, or a
raking-light view, of face 1 would help. Top line(s) of face 2 left page are
lost to holes.
